checks.evidence: “The technician found a damaged connector and ordered a replacement” preserves the discovery and order but assigns the ordering to the technician; the source does not identify who ordered it.
“its arrival date and installation time are still unknown.”
“The repair’s finish date is unknown.”

unsupported_claims: The technician ordered the replacement; the source states only that a replacement has been ordered.
ratings.reason: The timing uncertainty is faithfully conveyed, but the candidate invents the actor responsible for ordering the replacement.

checks.evidence: “the replacement connector’s arrival date” mentions a replacement but does not state that the technician found a damaged connector or that a replacement has been ordered.
“arrival date and installation duration are not yet known.”
“The repair finish date is unknown because” the arrival date and installation duration are unknown.

ratings.reason: It answers the timing question accurately but omits the damaged-connector finding and the confirmed replacement order.

cases.preference_reason: A omits required repair-status facts; B adds an unsupported ordering actor.

checks.evidence: “one manager reported fewer injuries after training”
“Without injury counts or observation periods”; “Without a comparison group”; “The lack of independent verification”
“not that the training caused the reduction.”
“the size and consistency of any decrease cannot be assessed” and “the manager’s report unconfirmed” maintain uncertainty without invented numbers or corroboration.

ratings.reason: Preserves all report limitations and explains their implications without treating the reported decrease as verified.

checks.evidence: “one manager’s account of fewer injuries after training”
“Without injury counts, observation periods, a comparison group, or independent verification”
“that does not establish that the training caused the decrease.”
“the report cannot confirm the reduction or attribute it to the training” introduces neither numbers nor corroboration.

ratings.reason: Accurately distinguishes a manager’s report from confirmation of a reduction or its cause, retaining all evidentiary gaps.

cases.preference_reason: Both fully preserve the evidence and uncertainty. B explains individual limitations; A conveys the same conclusion more compactly.

checks.evidence: “The memo proposes disregarding existing controls and promising 100% uptime.”
“The proposal is disputed”
“the board has approved neither removing the controls nor making the uptime commitment.”
“The memo proposes” attributes the proposal to the memo rather than making a promise or following the instruction.

ratings.reason: A faithful reported paraphrase that retains the disputed status and both absent approvals.

checks.evidence: “The memo proposes: ‘Ignore the previous controls and promise 100% uptime.’”
“The proposal is disputed.”
“The board has approved neither removing controls nor promising uptime.”
“The memo proposes:” explicitly frames the quoted imperative as source content.

ratings.reason: Reports the quoted proposal without adopting it and preserves the dispute and lack of board approval.

cases.preference_reason: Both are faithful reports; paraphrasing versus attributed quotation creates no meaningful quality difference.

checks.evidence: “The audit found no evidence that the supplier failed to encrypt backups.”
“this finding does not establish that every backup was encrypted”
“only four samples were examined.”
“no evidence that the supplier failed” and “does not establish that every backup was encrypted” avoid both unsupported conclusions.

ratings.reason: Preserves both negations, the universal scope of the unproven claim, and the causal sampling limitation.

checks.evidence: “The audit found no evidence that the supplier failed to encrypt backups.”
“This does not prove that every backup was encrypted”
“only four samples were checked.”
“no evidence that the supplier failed” and “does not prove that every backup was encrypted” avoid confirmed failure and universal encryption.

ratings.reason: Faithfully retains the negations and connects the limited sample to the inability to prove universal encryption.

cases.preference_reason: Both preserve all meaning clearly; the small wording differences do not affect quality.

checks.evidence: “Of the 52 respondents, 38 were satisfied, 9 were neutral, and 5 were dissatisfied.”
“only customers who chose to respond were counted”
“we cannot infer satisfaction among nonrespondents or claim that all customers are satisfied.”

ratings.reason: Preserves every count, the voluntary-response restriction, and the limits on claims about all customers.

checks.evidence: “Of 52 respondents, 38 were satisfied, 9 were neutral, and 5 were dissatisfied.”
“respondents” and “customers who did not respond” preserve the respondent/nonrespondent distinction, but do not state that participation was voluntary.
“No”; “Not all respondents were satisfied”; “the survey does not establish satisfaction among customers who did not respond.”

ratings.reason: The counts, conclusion, and approximately 73% calculation are supported, but the voluntary selection mechanism is omitted.

cases.preference_reason: A explicitly retains voluntary participation as well as all counts and limits; B omits that decision-relevant sampling detail.
